title: What Do Recycling Arrows Really Mean?

fin.big: Simplified illustrations. Check your local recycling rules.
fin.small: Sources: US EPA, Plastics: Material-Specific Data (2018 data); FTC Green Guides, 16 CFR 260.12

parts: That little triangle of arrows does not mean it gets recycled.
It is a code. Stay to see where it turns into a promise.
The number inside just tells you which plastic it is.
Like PET, the plastic of drink bottles.
It began as an industry code.
So how much plastic actually gets recycled in America?
In twenty eighteen, the EPA counted just eight point seven percent.
PET bottles and jars: about twenty-nine percent. But where the arrows sit changes everything.
Put them on the front, near the brand, and that counts as a promise.
A promise that you can recycle it.
Unless sixty percent of buyers have somewhere to recycle it, the label is supposed to say so.
Hidden on the bottom, it promises nothing.
Check your town's list, not the arrows. Follow for tomorrow's mystery.
